name: Velora
description: Velora is a precisely calibrated GABAergic modulator and mild dopaminergic activator designed to eliminate social anxiety while preserving full cognitive function. Unlike alcohol or crude anxiolytics, Velora does not impair judgment, speech, or coordination — it simply removes the fear. Users report being fully themselves, without the internal friction that usually mediates social interaction. It is the most widely used social compound in GLMZ.
effects: Complete elimination of social anxiety without sedation
Heightened conversational fluency and genuine interest in others
Increased candor — inhibitions lower without judgment impairing
side_effects: Excessive candor — users sometimes disclose things they would not sober
Mild disinhibition can escalate in high-stakes social situations
Next-day mild anxiety rebound in regular users
Tolerance builds quickly — social anxiety returns worse without the drug for heavy users
Can be combined with other compounds to lower resistance to coercive questioning
cultural_context: Velora is so ubiquitous that its use is assumed at most social events — not disclosing that you're not on it is considered a minor social rudeness in some Tier 3-4 circles. The Shelf uses a cruder generic version called 'the Open' that has stronger disinhibition and worse rebounds. There is an ongoing cultural debate about whether GLMZ's famous social cohesion is genuine or pharmaceutical. Corporate HR departments have been caught using Velora in catering at negotiation events; the legal cases are still ongoing.
story_hooks: A journalist discovers that a major political summit was catered with Velora-laced beverages — the resulting treaty may have been signed under pharmaceutical coercion, and the implications for three corporate territories are explosive

A Velora-dependent Tier 3 professional realizes he has not had a genuine unmedicated social interaction in four years and cannot remember who he is without the drug — he wants help getting off it, but the withdrawal is destroying his career

The newest Velora formula has a secondary compound that Novafold hasn't disclosed — one that makes users slightly more receptive to suggestions from authority figures, and someone in Novafold's chain of command sold the modification to a third party
